questions.solution:

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = \left|$\begin{cases}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & - 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = 0 + 4 + 8$

$⇒ f\left(0\right) = 12$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = \left|$\begin{cases}x^{3} & 2x^{2} + 1 & 1 + 3x \\ 3x^{2} + 2 & 2x & x^{3} + 6 \\ 3x^{2} - 1 & 0 & 2x\end{cases}$\right| + \left|$\begin{cases}x^{3} & 2x^{2} + 1 & 1 + 3x \\ 6x & 2 & 3x^{2} \\ x^{3} - x & 4 & x^{2} - 2\end{cases}$\right| + \left|$\begin{cases}3x^{2} & 4x & 3 \\ 3x^{2} + 2 & 2x & x^{3} + 6 \\ x^{3} - x & 4 & x^{2} - 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(0\right) = \left|$\begin{cases}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 6 \\ - 1 & 0 & 0\end{cases}$\right| + \left|$\begin{cases}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & - 2\end{cases}$\right| + \left|$\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & - 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ f^{'} \left(0\right) = 0 - \left($0 + 6\right) + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + $3\left($8\right)$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($0\right) = - 6 + 24 = 18$

$⇒ $2f\left($0\right) + f^{'}\left($0\right) = 42$

$

questions.solution:
Given,

\left($\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & \gamma\end{cases}$\right)\left($\begin{cases}2 & 10 & 8 \\ 9 & 3 & 8 \\ 8 & 4 & 8\end{cases}$\right) = \left($\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}$\right)$

$⇒ \left($\begin{cases}2\alpha + 9\beta + 8\gamma & 10\alpha + 3\beta + 4\gamma & 8\alpha + 8\beta + 8\gamma\end{cases}$\right) = \left($\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 0\end{cases}$\right)$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$2\alpha + 2\beta + 8\gamma = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

$10\alpha ++3\beta ++4\gamma =0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$8\alpha +$+8\beta +$+8\gamma =0 \ldots \left(3\right)$

Now from \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($3\right)$ by cross multiplication we get,

\dfrac{α}{1} = \dfrac{β}{6} = \dfrac{γ}{- 7} =$k ⇒ $\alpha =$k, $\beta =$6k, $\gamma = -$7k$

Point $P \left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right)$lie on the plane $2x + 4y + 3z = 5 ⇒ 2\alpha +$+4\beta +$+3\gamma =5$

$⇒ 2k + 24k - 21k = 5$

$⇒ k = 1$

Hence,~$6\alpha +$+9\beta +$+7\gamma =6k + 54k - 49k = 11k = 11$.

$

questions.q:
Let $A = \left[{a}_{ij}\right]~be a $3 $\times$3$ matrix, where ${a}_{ij} = \left\{$\begin{cases}1 & , & ifi = j \\ - x & , & if \left|i - j\right| = 1 \\ 2x + 1 & , & otherwise\end{cases}$\right
Let a function $f: R \to R$ be defined as $f \left(x\right) = det \left($A\right)$. Then the sum of maximum and minimum values of~$f$~on $R$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

${a}_{ij} = \left\{$\begin{cases}1 & , & ifi = j \\ - x & , & if \left|i - j\right| = 1 \\ 2x + 1 & , & otherwise\end{cases}$\right

Then,

$A = \left[$\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } - x \text{ and } 2x + 1 \\ - x \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } - x \\ 2x + 1 \text{ and } - x \text{ and } 1\end{cases}$\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = \left(1 - x^{2}\right) + x \left(-$x + 2x^{2} + x\right) + \left($2x + 1\right)\left($x^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = 1 - x^{2} + 2x^{3} + \left(2x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 2x\right) + \left(x^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = f \left(x\right) = 4x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 4x$

$⇒ f^{'}\left(x\right) = 4\left(3x^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

For maxima or minima,~$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3x^{2} - 2x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = 1, $\dfrac{- 1}{3}

Now,

$f^{' '} \left(x\right) = 4 \left(6x - 2\right)$

$f^{' '}\left(1\right) = 4 \left(6 \cdot1 - 2\right) = 16 > 0$( point of minima)

$f^{' '}\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$=4\left(6 \cdot \left(- $\dfrac{1}{3}\right) -$2\right) = - 16 < 0$~( point of maxima)

Hence, required sum is

$f \left(1\right) + f \left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)

$= - 4 + $\dfrac{20}{27} = - \dfrac{88}{27}

$

questions.q:
If the system of equations

$x + y + az = b$

$2x + 5y + 2z = 6$

$x + 2y + 3z = 3$

has infinitely many solutions, then $2a + 3b$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given system of equations are

$x + y + az = b . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$2x + 5y + 2z = 6 . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

$x + 2y + 3z = 3 . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

It is given that the system of equations have infinite solutions.

$⇒ ∆ = 0$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & a \\ 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(15 - 4\right) - 1\left(6 - 2\right) + a\left(4 - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ a = 7$~

Also, we have~$⇒ {∆}_{1} = 0$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}b & 1 & a \\ 6 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ b\left(15 - 4\right) - 1\left(18 - 6\right) + 7\left(12 - 15\right) = 0$

$⇒ b = 3$

$∴ a = 7, b = 3$~

$∴ 2a + 3b= 14 + 9 = 23

Hence, this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: For real numbers $\alpha$~and $\beta,$~consider the following system of linear equations: $x + y - z = 2, x + 2y + \alphaz = 1$~and~$2x - y + z = \beta .$~If the system has infinite solutions, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given system of linear equations are& $x + y - z = 2, x + 2y + \alphaz = 1, 2x - y + z = \beta$

Using Cramer Rule, we can say for infinite solutions

$\Delta = {Δ}_{1} = {Δ}_{2} = {Δ}_{3} = 0$

Here,~$\Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

Apply~${R}_{1} ↔ {R}_{1} + {R}_{3}$

$⇒ \left|$\begin{cases}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(2 + \alpha\right) = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = - 2$

And~${Δ}_{2} = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 2 & - 1 \\ 1 & 1 & - 2 \\ 2 & \beta & 1\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(1 + 2\beta\right) - 2\left(1 + 4\right) - \left(\beta - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ \beta - 7 = 0$

$⇒ \beta = 7$

$∴ \alpha + \beta = 5$

questions.q:
Let& $p$ and $p + 2$~be prime numbers and let
$\Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}p ! & \left(p + 1\right) ! & \left(p + 2\right) ! \\ \left(p + 1\right) ! & \left(p + 2\right) ! & \left(p + 3\right) ! \\ \left(p + 2\right) ! & \left(p + 3\right) ! & \left(p + 4\right) !\end{cases}$\right|$
Then the sum of the maximum values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, such that $p^{α}$~and \left(p + 2\right)\beta$~divide $\Delta$, is _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\Delta = \left|$\begin{cases}P ! & \left(P + 1\right) ! & \left(P + 2\right) ! \\ \left(P + 1\right) ! & \left(P + 2\right) ! & \left(P + 3\right) ! \\ \left(P + 2\right) ! & \left(P + 3\right) ! & \left(P + 4\right) !\end{cases}$\right|$

Now using the factorial concept and taking common terms we get,

$⇒ \Delta = P ! \left(P + 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right) ! \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ P + 1 & P + 2 & P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) & \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}$\right|$

Now on solving determinant we get, \left|$\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ P + 1 & P + 2 & P + 3 \\ \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right) & \left(P + 3\right)\left(P + 2\right) & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}$\right|$

Using operation~${C}_{1} \to {C}_{1} - {C}_{2} \text{ and } {C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{3}$

\left|$\begin{cases}0 & 0 & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & P + 3 \\ - 2P - 4 & - 2P - 6 & \left(P + 4\right)\left(P + 3\right)\end{cases}$\right|$

$= 2P + 6 - \left(2P + 4\right) = 2$

Now putting the value of determinant we get,

$⇒ \Delta = 2P ! \left(P + 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right) !$

$⇒ \Delta = 2P^{3}\left(P - 1\right) ! \left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right) ! \left(P + 2\right)\left(P + 1\right)\left(P - 1\right) !$

Which is divisible by~$P^{α}$~and~\left(P + 2\right)\beta$

So,~$\alpha = 3, \beta = 1$

$

Let& ${D}_{k} = \left|
1 2k 2k - 1
nn^{2} + n + 2n^{2}
nn^{2} + nn^{2} + n + 2
\right|$. If~$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = 96$, then~$n$& is equal to _________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that& ${D}_{k} = \left|
1 2k 2k - 1
nn^{2} + n + 2n^{2}
nn^{2} + nn^{2} + n + 2
\right|$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = \left|$\begin{cases}∑ 1 & 2 ∑ k & 2 ∑ k - ∑ 1 \\ n & n^{2} + n + 2 & n^{2} \\ n & n^{2} + n & n^{2} + n + 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = \left|$\begin{cases}n & 2\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} & 2\left(\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}\right) - n \\ n & n^{2} + n + 2 & n^{2} \\ n & n^{2} + n & n^{2} + n + 2\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = \left|$\begin{cases}n & n\left(n + 1\right) & n^{2} \\ n & n^{2} + n + 2 & n^{2} \\ n & n^{2} + n & n^{2} + n + 2\end{cases}$\right|$

${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}$~and~${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{3}$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = \left|$\begin{cases}0 & - 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & - n - 2 \\ n & n^{2} + n & n^{2} + n + 2\end{cases}$\right|$

Expand the determinant along~${R}_{1}$.

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{D}_{k} = 2\left(\left(- n\right)\left(- n - 2\right)\right) = 96$

$⇒ n^{2} + 2n = 48$

$⇒ n = 6, - 8$

So,~$n = 6$

Hence this is the required answer.

questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left|$\begin{cases}\sin^{2}x & - 2 + \cos^{2}x & \cos 2x \\ 2 + \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & \cos 2x \\ \sin^{2}x & \cos^{2}x & 1 + \cos 2x\end{cases}$\right|$

{R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}
{R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{3}
\right)$

$= - 2 \left(\cos^{2}x\right) + 2 \left($2 + 2\cos 2x + \sin^{2}x\right)$

$= 4 + 4\cos 2x - 2 \left(\cos^{2}x - \sin^{2}x\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = 4 + 2\cos 2x$

So,~$f\left(x\right)max = 4 + 2 = 6$

$
